alignments.note: Waw rendered by the connective *Then* (rule 14; the list is read off the ASV).
Inflected verb takes its English subject pronoun and lexical verb (rule 17), headed on *looked* (rule 24).
Conjunction to *and*.
Presentative particle to *behold*.
Preposition rendered *in* (rule 11).

Construct noun; the ASV writes two *the*s, so the article on the rectum takes the one before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one (rule 29).
Article on the rectum takes the *the* written before *cherubim* (rule 29).

Comparative particle rendered by the whole frame *as it were*; the supplied *it were* is the construction's copula (rule 20) and joins the particle's unit, headed on *as*. Competing reading: give only *as* to the particle and treat *it were* as a copula on the following nominal predicate.
Head noun of the nominal expression, which licenses the indefinite *a* (rule 15); the construct chain is rendered attributively (rule 28).
Rectum rendered attributively as *sapphire* (rule 28).
Comparative particle to *as*.
Construct noun with a supplied *the*, no article morpheme present (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes *of* (rule 19) with a supplied *the* on the inner construct (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes *of*; the indefinite *a* belongs to the noun (rules 19, 15).

review_notes: The two comparative כְּ phrases are aligned in place after the main clause's verb and prepositional complement, so several units are discontinuous in target order (rule 25).
